q1.answer: Backstage decided that any fetch or XMLHttpRequest in tests should be mocked with msw rather than mocking fetch directly (as react-testing-library recommends), so request mocking is declared as express-style route handlers and the client's real fetch path is exercised. The cost accepted is a little more test code.

q2.answer: ADR014 (which supersedes ADR013) says frontend plugins should use fetchApiRef rather than an HTTP library, and that clients should accept an injected fetch implementation so callers can add auth or other information and track metrics in a cross-platform way; it also reduces the burden of supporting several HTTP packages. ADR013's node-fetch/cross-fetch guidance no longer applies.

q3.answer: Luxon is Backstage's standard date library for formatting and calculations (such as relative time like 'a day ago') that native Date doesn't cover well. Moment.js was rejected because of its large bundle size and mutable state, and because it is being sunset; Luxon is immutable and uses Intl, and having one library keeps bundles smaller.

q4.answer: Backstage avoids React.FC/React.SFC in new code, following create-react-app's removal of it: FC adds children props implicitly and does not support generic types on children. Instead, props are typed explicitly on a plain function, with children declared only when needed.

q5.answer: Every exported symbol has to be traceable through index files up to src/index.ts, and each index file re-exports only from its immediate children, so you can tell what a package exposes by walking up the index files. Reaching into deep files would break that traceability. Index files use `export *` for child indexes and list exports explicitly when re-exporting from non-index files.
